summary: Haines Airport (HNS) is a medium-sized public airport serving the community of Haines on the Chilkat Peninsula in southeastern Alaska. Situated along the Lynn Canal, it provides essential access for a town that is otherwise reachable only by a long, winding road or the Alaska Marine Highway ferry system. The airport is particularly notable as a gateway for visitors heading to the Chilkat Bald Eagle Preserve, one of the largest gatherings of bald eagles in the world.
faqs:
Q: What airlines serve Haines Airport?
A: Haines Airport is primarily served by small regional carriers offering scheduled flights, with charter services also commonly available for travelers heading to remote areas.

Q: How far is the airport from downtown Haines?
A: The airport is located just a short drive from the town center of Haines, making it convenient for visitors to reach local accommodations and the waterfront.

Q: Is the airport open year-round?
A: Yes, Haines Airport operates throughout the year, though winter weather conditions can occasionally affect flight schedules.

Q: Are there rental cars available at the airport?
A: Transportation options from the airport are limited; many visitors arrange rental cars or shuttle services in advance through local providers in town.
transport_tips: Renting a car in advance is recommended, as on-site rental options at Haines Airport are limited and local providers often arrange pickups from the terminal. Taxi services and pre-booked shuttles are available for transfers to downtown Haines and the ferry terminal. The scenic drive to Haines from the airport is short but offers immediate views of the surrounding mountains and Chilkat Inlet.
local_tip: Pack a pair of binoculars in your carry-on — Haines is famous as one of the best places in North America to observe bald eagles, especially during the late fall and early winter congregation at the nearby Chilkat Bald Eagle Preserve, which is just minutes from the airport.
